findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The WebAuthn setup gate in challenge(context, error, field) is inverted from user==null to user!=null, so error pages for an unidentified (invalid/unknown) username no longer carry the passkey conditional-UI data that the previous code explicitly set up. On a realm with passkeys enabled using the combined username+password form, a passkey-only user who mistypes their username gets an error page without the webauthn form/autocomplete markup and must restart the flow to use their passkey; additionally the re-rendered error page now differs structurally (webauthn markup present for existing users via badPasswordHandler, absent for unknown usernames), which is a response-difference username-enumeration oracle (previously present in the opposite direction, so the diff flips rather than removes the asymmetry).

[ADVISORY] isConditionalPasskeysEnabled gates passkey-based re-authentication (prompt=login / step-up) only on the realm passkeys-enabled flag and a non-null user, with no check that the realm WebAuthn passwordless policy enforces user verification, so a re-authentication can be satisfied by a passkey assertion without user verification when the policy is set to preferred/discouraged. In a realm that enables passkeys without USER_VERIFICATION_OPTION_REQUIRED, an attacker with brief access to an unlocked device (or any passive possession of the authenticator) satisfies prompt=login re-authentication with no biometric/PIN prompt, defeating the step-up guarantee that re-authentication is supposed to provide; the diff newly enables this path (previously passkeys never completed during re-authentication) and no UV requirement is enforced at this gate.

[ADVISORY] The 'webauthn button absent' check passes via a catch-all `catch (Exception nsee)` that swallows any exception, and the `MatcherAssert.assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue())` line inside the try can never succeed (findElement either throws or returns a non-null WebElement), so the check relies entirely on exception type and treats every non-NoSuchElement failure (WebDriverException, stale element, page-not-rendered) as the expected outcome. If the login page fails to render or the driver throws a timing/stale-element error, the test silently passes instead of failing, masking a real regression in the passkeys-disabled re-authentication path; note this is also a precision regression versus the pattern this PR deletes in the sibling file, which used the precise `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)`.

[ADVISORY] Second occurrence of the same false-confidence pattern: the re-authentication webauthn-absence check is guarded by `catch (Exception nsee)` with an unreachable `assertThat(..., nullValue())` line, so any WebDriverException other than NoSuchElementException is reported as 'expected'. A broken re-authentication page (e.g., the 'Please re-authenticate' page fails to render the login form) makes findElement throw a non-NoSuchElement exception that is swallowed, so the assertion that passkeys UI is NOT shown during re-authentication without passkeys passes vacuously and a regression in UsernamePasswordForm.challenge goes undetected.

[ADVISORY] The newly added call to `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)` in the passkey-failure error path (createErrorResponse) is never exercised by any test in this diff — none of the three changed test files (PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.java, PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java, PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java) simulates a failed passkey authentication during re-authentication, so this new branch has zero coverage. A regression in the new behavior (e.g., the call being dropped or the auth-note check failing so the username field is shown and registration offered after a failed passkey attempt during re-auth) ships silently, reproducing exactly the class of re-authentication UX bug this PR set out to fix.

[ADVISORY] No test in this diff asserts the actual effect of `setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError` — neither USERNAME_HIDDEN nor REGISTRATION_DISABLED is ever checked after a failed re-authentication; the closest test, webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey (~lines 372-381), asserts only the 'Invalid password.' error text and that the webauth form is still present. If the two form attributes stop being set (e.g., the Boolean.parseBoolean auth-note parse breaks or the auth-note key drifts after the constant was made public and is now writable from other packages), every re-auth test in the diff still passes while end users get a full login form (with registration link) instead of the hidden-username re-authentication form after a failed password attempt.

goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(context, error, field)`, the condition for calling `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` changed from `context.getUser() == null && ... isPasskeysEnabled()` to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, and `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` explicitly requires `user != null`. This is a verifiable inversion: when the username is unknown/invalid (so `context.getUser()` stays null), the error challenge will no longer populate the WebAuthn conditional-UI/passkeys form attributes/markup that previously would have been set up in that case.

In a realm that enables passkeys without USER_VERIFICATION_OPTION_REQUIRED, an attacker with brief access to an unlocked device (or any passive possession of the authenticator) satisfies prompt=login re-authentication with no biometric/PIN prompt, defeating the step-up guarantee that re-authentication is supposed to provide; the diff newly enables this path (previously passkeys never completed during re-authentication) and no UV requirement is enforced at this gate.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does newly enable conditional passkeys during re-authentication by calling `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true (UsernamePasswordForm), and that gate only checks `webauthnAuth != null`, `webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`, and `user != null`—it does not check any WebAuthn policy/user-verification requirement. However, the diff does not show how user verification is enforced (or not) during the actual WebAuthn assertion/validation, so the claim that re-authentication can be satisfied without UV (and that this "defeats" step-up guarantees) cannot be verified from the provided changes alone; it’s a concrete, diff-grounded security/design concern rather than a clearly provable defect in this diff.

adjudication.rationale: In PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey(), the “webauthn button not available” checks are implemented as `try { driver.findElement(...); assertThat(..., nullValue()); fail(...); } catch (Exception nsee) { /* expected */ }` twice. Since `findElement` never returns null, the `assertThat(..., nullValue())` can’t succeed; absence is detected only by an exception. Moreover, catching broad `Exception` will treat any RuntimeException from Selenium/WebDriver (e.g., WebDriverException due to timing/page-render issues) as the expected outcome, potentially masking real regressions in the test path instead of failing explicitly. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test robustness issue (not product behavior).

A broken re-authentication page (e.g., the 'Please re-authenticate' page fails to render the login form) makes findElement throw a non-NoSuchElement exception that is swallowed, so the assertion that passkeys UI is NOT shown during re-authentication without passkeys passes vacuously and a regression in UsernamePasswordForm.challenge goes undetected.

adjudication.rationale: In PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey(), the absence check is implemented as `try { assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...); } catch (Exception nsee) { /* expected */ }`. Since `findElement` either returns a non-null WebElement or throws, the `assertThat(..., nullValue())` can never legitimately pass, and the broad `catch (Exception)` will treat *any* WebDriver/Runtime exception (not just `NoSuchElementException`) as “expected”, potentially hiding real page/rendering failures and letting the test pass for the wrong reason. This is a real, diff-grounded test robustness issue, not a production behavior defect.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new call in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse(...)` to `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)`, which only runs on the passkey-failure error path. The updated/added tests in `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest`, `PasskeysUsernameFormTest`, and `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest` cover successful passkey logins and some password failures during re-authentication, but none of them simulates a *failed WebAuthn/passkey authentication* during re-authentication that would exercise `createErrorResponse(...)` and thus this new branch. This is a specific, diff-grounded gap in coverage for newly added UX-affecting logic, not a direct defect by itself.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new nontrivial logic in `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(...)` that sets `LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN` and `LoginFormsProvider.REGISTRATION_DISABLED` when the auth note `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` parses to true, and wires it into error paths (`AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler` and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse`). The added/updated tests exercise re-authentication and failed password flows, but they only assert error text and/or presence of the webauthn form (e.g., `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey` checks "Invalid password." and `//form[@id='webauth']`), and none assert the form-state effects (hidden username / registration disabled) that this helper is intended to preserve during re-auth. This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap for the newly introduced behavior rather than a proven functional defect in the diff itself.
